deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the opening of Riemann's formal Latin petition to the Göttingen Philosophical Faculty for admission to the doctorate, written in fair copy in 1851. The next page dates it to October 1851; the crossed-out day reads 29 October.

Title block: 'Ab amplissimo philosophorum ordine ea, qua par est, reverentia, doctoris gradum petit G. F. B. Riemann Breselenzius, stud. math.' This means: 'From the most distinguished order of philosophers, with due reverence, G. F. B. Riemann of Breselenz, student of mathematics, requests the degree of doctor.'

Salutation: 'Decane spectatissime, professores honorificentissimi!' This means: 'Most esteemed Dean, most honourable professors!'

Body, continued on the next page: 'Mathematicae et physicae studio quum per quinquennium deditus fuerim, jam peto a Vobis, viri maxime venerandi, ut ob meam harum artium scientiam, quae sentio quam [sit exigua], philosophiae doctorem me creetis.' This means: 'Since I have devoted myself for five years to the study of mathematics and physics, I now ask of you, most venerable men, that on account of my knowledge of these arts, which I feel to be slight, you create me Doctor of Philosophy.'

The next page goes on to submit, as a specimen of worthiness, a dissertation 'in jaciendis fundamentis theoriae generalis functionum complexae quantitatis variabilis' ('on laying the foundations of a general theory of functions of a complex variable quantity'). This is the 1851 Inaugural Dissertation, 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'.

Context: the previous page of the bundle is a German draft of the dissertation's Dirichlet-principle argument (§§16–18 area). That draft covers minimising Ω = ∫((∂u/∂x)²+(∂u/∂y)²)dT under fixed boundary values, which yields Δu = 0 and uniqueness. This page itself carries only the administrative cover letter that accompanied the dissertation.

The 'quinquennium' (five years) matches Riemann's studies of 1846–1851 at Göttingen and Berlin.

results.what: Formal Latin petition for the doctoral degree accompanying the 1851 dissertation on complex function theory (biographical/administrative document, no mathematical content)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann, 1851 (known biographical fact; dissertation submitted to Göttingen, defended December 1851)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the purely administrative cover petition for Riemann's well-known 1851 doctoral dissertation. It has no mathematical content, and both the dissertation and the circumstances of the doctorate are thoroughly documented.

checkable.asserts: The date 'MDCCCLI' on the following page equals 1851, the year of the dissertation.
The crossed-out day 'XXIX' on the following page denotes the 29th (of October).

transcription_corrections: The transcription is accurate. 'Breselenzius' (of Breselenz, Riemann's birthplace) is correctly read; the 'z' carries a small mark beneath it.

Faint mirror-image text visible in the upper half is bleed-through of the verso/next page ('sit exigua, philosophiae doctorem me creetis ... G. F. B. Riemann, stud. math.'). It is not part of this page's text.
A folio number '76' is pencilled in the right margin near the top; it is omitted in the transcription.
The last line breaks off at 'quae sentio quam' and continues on the next page with 'sit exigua'.
